mainTopic: When a גט must be written for a specific woman, and רבא's contradictions about whether intent 'not of its kind' (like חולין) affects קדשים
overview: The amud opens by looking for a source that a גט written סתם, for no particular woman, is invalid. The גמרא tries three 'יתר על כן' clauses of the משנה in גיטין and pushes each one off: the first two were written for someone else, and the third can be explained by אין ברירה. The proof finally comes from טופסי גיטין, where even 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם' must be left blank. Next, רבא quotes רב: a חטאת slaughtered for an עולה is פסול, but slaughtered for חולין it is כשר, so only intent 'of its own kind' ruins it. He sets this against a גט written for a גויה, which is פסול. He answers that if you remove the foreign intent you are left with סתם, and a סתם גט is פסול while סתם קדשים are כשר. He then sets רב against the ברייתא that a כלי שטף protects inside a כלי חרס. He answers that חולין next to קדשים is like a partition in an oven, which has no effect at all. The גמרא brings the משנה about a divided oven and a broken barrel, where רבי אליעזר argues with a קל וחומר and the חכמים begin to reject it. Their reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the man who shares a name with his townsman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a clause from the משנה: a גט written by one man for his wife cannot be used by another man with the same name and the same wife's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover: a man wrote a גט to divorce his wife and then changed his mind. Someone from his town found him and said, 'My name is like your name, and my wife's name is like your wife's name.' That גט is invalid for the second man to divorce with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line of the משנה as a proof that a גט must be written for one specific woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every name in the גט fits the second couple perfectly, and it was written for the purpose of divorce. It is still invalid. So the proof seems to be that a גט not written for this exact woman does not work, even if it was written for divorce in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Moreover, going even further (the משנה adds a stronger case)

phrases.english: Moreover,
if he wrote a גט to divorce his wife and changed his mind,
and a man from his town found him and said to him:
'My name is the same as your name,
and my wife's name is the same as your wife's name,'
it is invalid to divorce with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, כָּתַב לְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְנִמְלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search for a source, from earlier in the sugya, that a סתם גט is invalid.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט not written for a specific woman (סתם) is invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in גיטין: the townsman with the same name cannot use the first man's גט

steps.title: Pushback: that גט was set aside for the first man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. That גט was written for the first man's divorce, so it is not a סתם case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is different there, because the גט was designated for that man's divorce!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the townsman case, the גט was not blank or general. It was written for a specific other divorce. That may be the only reason it fails, so a גט written סתם might still be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a divorce

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה's ruling is wrong. It agrees the גט is invalid. It only says this case does not prove the rule about a סתם גט.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
because it was designated
for the sake of that man's divorce!
phrases.notes: 'That man' is the first husband, the one who wrote the גט and changed his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the ruling of the משנה stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is a גט written for someone else, not a גט written סתם.

steps.title: Proof from the man with two wives who have the same name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the next clause: a man who wrote a גט for his older wife cannot use it for his younger wife with the identical name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from this: Moreover, if a man has two wives with the same name and he wrote a גט to divorce the older one, he may not divorce the younger one with it.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first proof was pushed away, the גמרא brings a new proof from the following line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here it is the very same husband, and the names match exactly, yet the גט still cannot be used for the other wife. This seems to show even more strongly that a גט must be written for one particular woman.

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from this:
Moreover,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁמוֹתֵיהֶן שָׁווֹת –
phrases.english: if he has two wives whose names are the same,
and he wrote a גט to divorce the older one,
he may not divorce the younger one with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָא: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 1 with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט not written for a specific woman (סתם) is invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in גיטין: a גט written for the older wife cannot divorce the younger wife with the same name

steps.title: Pushback: that גט was set aside for the other wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way. That גט was written for the older wife's divorce, so it is not a סתם case either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is different there, because the גט was designated for that other woman's divorce!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof with the same answer it gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the גט was written for a definite other person, here the older wife. A גט written for someone else failing does not prove that a גט written סתם fails. So the גמרא keeps looking, and step 5 tries the next clause.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified, written without naming who it is for

steps.whatToRemember: The first two 'יתר על כן' cases show that a גט written for someone else is invalid. They do not prove that a גט written סתם is invalid, so the גמרא tries the next clause in step 5.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
because it was designated
for the sake of that woman's divorce!
phrases.notes: 'That woman' is the older wife. Notice the wording changes from דהָהוּא (that man) to דהָהִיא (that woman).

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִינְּתִיק לֵיהּ לְשֵׁם גֵּירוּשִׁין דְּהָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 using the same reasoning as step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the משנה's ruling stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The גט was written for a specific other woman, not סתם.

steps.title: Trying the 'whichever wife I want' clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a third clause from the same משנה: a man tells the scribe to write a גט so he can divorce whichever of his two same-named wives he chooses. That גט is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from this: Moreover, if he told the scribe, 'Write, and I will divorce whichever one I want,' the גט is unfit to divorce with.
steps.whatsHappening: After two failed proofs, the גמרא tries the next clause of the same משנה. A גט written for 'whichever wife I choose' is invalid, so maybe that shows an unspecified גט is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the גט was not written for one particular wife, so it seems closer to a סתם case. If it is still פסול, that would suggest a גט must be written for a specific woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Moreover; even more than that (the משנה adds a stronger case)
And for whichever one I want

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from this:
Moreover,
if he said to the scribe: Write,
and I will divorce whichever one I want,
it is unfit to divorce with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 rejected the older/younger wife clause, the גמרא moves to the next clause in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט written סתם, not for a specific woman, is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין: 'Write, and I will divorce whichever one I want' is פסול.

steps.title: Rejected: no retroactive choosing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. That case may be invalid only because of אין ברירה: we cannot decide afterward which wife the גט was 'really' written for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because there is no retroactive clarification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 5. That case might be invalid for a different reason, so it does not prove anything about a plain סתם גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case the גט was written for one of two real women, and we cannot later pick which one it was for (אין ברירה). It may have been meant for the other wife. A truly סתם גט was not tied to anyone else, so it might still be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: deciding later what was intended earlier

steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not say a סתם גט is valid. It only says this case cannot prove it is invalid, because something else could explain the ruling.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
because there is no retroactive clarification!
phrases.notes: He means we can't say afterward, 'it turns out this גט was for this wife all along.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the 'whichever I want' clause only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling can be explained by אין ברירה, because the גט may have belonged to the other wife. That has nothing to do with a סתם גט.

steps.title: Proof from blank גט forms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה about טופסי גיטין: a scribe writing forms in advance must leave blank the names, witnesses and date. שמואל adds that even the key phrase 'you are permitted to any man' must be left blank. This shows a גט not written for a specific woman is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from this: One who writes forms for גיטין must leave space for the man, the woman, the witnesses and the date. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: He must also leave space for 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about scribes who prepare גט forms ahead of time. This proof stands, and nothing rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A form is written for divorce in general but not for any particular woman. שמואל says even the central words of the גט cannot be pre-written, so they must be written for the specific woman. That shows a גט written סתם is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Pre-written forms of a גט, with the standard text
The place or blank space left for later writing
'You are hereby permitted to any man,' the central phrase of a גט

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a סתם גט is פסול comes from טופסי גיטין. Even the main words of the גט must be written for the specific woman, not in advance.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast רבא is working with: a גט written סתם is invalid, unlike קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from this:
One who writes forms of bills of divorce
must leave the space for the man
and the space for the woman and the space for the witnesses
and the space for the date.
And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
He must also leave the space for
'You are hereby permitted to any man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 rejected the last proof, the גמרא turns to a different משנה and finds a proof that holds.
steps.raayaObject: That a גט written סתם is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of טופסי גיטין in גיטין, together with שמואל's addition about 'הרי את מותרת לכל אדם'.

steps.title: A new contradiction: a חטאת slaughtered for עולה versus for חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises another contradiction. He cites רב: a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is פסול, but slaughtered for the sake of חולין it is כשר. That implies only intent 'of its own kind' ruins an offering. The other side of the contradiction comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: He further raised another contradiction: Did רב יהודה say in the name of רב that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is unfit, but slaughtered for the sake of חולין it is fit? Apparently intent of its own kind ruins it, and intent not of its kind does not ruin it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: רבא lays down the first half of a contradiction. This step sets up the conflict, and the clashing source comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Intending another קרבן, like an עולה, is the same 'kind' of thing and ruins the חטאת. Intending plain חולין meat is a different kind, so it is ignored. רבא draws that general rule from רב so he can contrast it with another statement.

keyTerms.meaning: He throws together two sources, meaning he points out a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only half of the contradiction. Don't look for the 'other side' here, because it comes in step 9.

phrases.english: He further raised another contradiction:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא, whose questions are being reported. Literally, 'he threw another matter.'

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit,
if he slaughtered it for the sake of non-sacred meat, it is fit;
apparently, intent of its own kind ruins it,
and intent not of its kind does not ruin it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The search for a source on a סתם גט is finished. A new contradiction from רבא begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב, brought by רב יהודה, about a חטאת slaughtered for עולה or for חולין, and the rule inferred from it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From רב's ruling we learn that only intent 'of its kind' ruins a קרבן. This will be set against another source that seems to say the opposite, which comes next.

steps.title: A גט written for a non-Jewish woman is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the other side of his contradiction: a גט written for a גויה is פסול, even though a גויה is not 'of its kind'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised a contradiction: any גט that was not written for the sake of the woman is invalid. That means even a גט written for the sake of a non-Jewish woman is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the contradiction he started in Step 8. He quotes a משנה about גיטין that seems to clash with רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב implied that only intent 'of its own kind' ruins an offering, so intent for חולין does no harm. But a גויה has nothing to do with divorce, so she is 'not of its kind', and still a גט written for her is פסול. So here intent that is not of its kind does ruin something.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them: the גמרא sets one source against another to show a contradiction
Not for the sake of the woman: a גט not written for the specific woman being divorced
A non-Jewish woman, who has no connection to the laws of גט

phrases.english: And he contrasted it: any bill of divorce that was written
not for the sake of the woman is invalid.
And even if written for the sake of a non-Jewish woman, it is also invalid!
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say this outright. רבא reads it from the word 'any': every גט not written for her is out, even one written for a גויה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the second half of the contradiction opened in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule taken from רב that only intent 'of its own kind' ruins something.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גויה is not 'of the kind' of a גט, yet intent for her makes the גט פסול. So intent that is not of its kind can ruin something.

steps.title: Take away the outside intent and see what remains
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves it: once the outside intent is removed, a גט is left as a סתם גט, which is פסול, while קדשים are left as סתם קדשים, which are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: with a גט, take away the non-Jewish woman and it is as if written with no one in mind, and an unspecified גט is invalid. With קדשים, take away the חולין and it is as if slaughtered with no specific intent, and unspecified offerings are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own contradiction. He shows that the two cases really follow the same logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Intent that is 'not of its kind' simply counts as nothing. What decides the case is the default (סתם) status. A סתם גט is פסול, as Step 7 proved from טופסי גיטין, but סתם קדשים are כשר. So the results differ even though the logic is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: And he resolved it: introduces an answer
Unspecified: done with no particular intent

steps.whatToRemember: Intent 'not of its kind' counts as no intent at all. A גט with no intent is פסול, but קדשים with no intent are כשר.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the גויה intent ruins the גט. It counts as nothing, and the גט is פסול only because a סתם גט is פסול anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle of 'remove it and see what is left', which explains why the same kind of outside intent leads to different results in different areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: And he resolved: a bill of divorce —
remove the non-Jewish woman from it,
and it is unspecified, and an unspecified one is invalid.
Sacrificial animals: remove the non-sacred intent from them,
and they are unspecified, and unspecified ones are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 8–9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the default (סתם) status of each area of halacha.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Intent for a גויה actively ruins the גט, which would clash with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Intent not of its kind counts as nothing in both cases. The difference comes from the fact that a סתם גט is פסול while סתם קדשים are כשר.

steps.title: Repeating רב's ruling to set up a new contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב's ruling about חטאת again, this time as the first side of a different contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised another contradiction: Did רב יהודה really say in the name of רב that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of an עולה is invalid, but slaughtered for the sake of חולין it is valid? So intent of its own kind ruins it, but intent not of its kind does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new move. רבא repeats רב's ruling so he can set it against a different source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote is the same as in Step 8, but now it serves a new contradiction. The point to hold onto is the conclusion drawn from it: something 'not of its kind' has no effect.

phrases.english: And he raised another contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Did רב יהודה say that רב said:
a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit,
but if he slaughtered it for the sake of non-sacred meat, it is fit;
apparently, what is of its kind ruins it,
and what is not of its kind does not ruin it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second contradiction by repeating רב's ruling from Step 8 for a new purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, and the rule drawn from it that only 'its own kind' has an effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the first side. The opposing source comes in the next step.

steps.title: A rinsable vessel protects inside an earthenware vessel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that food inside an inner vessel within a כלי חרס stays טהור, even when the inner vessel is a כלי שטף, which is not 'of the kind' of the earthenware.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: 'its interior', and not the interior of its interior. And even a vessel that is cleaned by rinsing protects!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the other side of the new contradiction: a ברייתא where something 'not of its kind' still makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס spreads טומאה only to what is in its own interior. A כלי שטף is not of the same kind as a כלי חרס, yet when it sits inside, it still stops the טומאה from reaching the food in it. So something not of its kind does have an effect, which clashes with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Its interior: the inside of a כלי חרס, which becomes טמא from within
The interior of its interior: inside another vessel that sits in the כלי חרס
A vessel purified by rinsing in a מקוה, such as one of metal or wood
Protects, saves its contents from טומאה

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'its interior' —
but not the interior of its interior,
and even a vessel cleaned by rinsing protects!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the opposing source for the contradiction set up in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule drawn from רב that what is 'not of its kind' has no effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כלי שטף is not of the kind of a כלי חרס, yet it changes the outcome by protecting the food inside it. So something not of its kind can have an effect.

steps.title: Non-sacred intent is like a partition in an oven
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction: חולין compared to קדשים is like a partition inside an oven, which has no effect at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא answers: non-sacred relative to sacred is like a partition relative to an oven. Just as a partition does nothing at all inside an oven, so too intent for חולין does nothing at all to קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from the previous step. He says intent for חולין is like a partition inside an oven, which does not count at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why a כלי שטף protects food inside a כלי חרס even though it is not 'of its kind', while חולין intent does not affect a קרבן. רבא suggests that a כלי שטף is still a real vessel, so it matters. חולין is totally foreign to קדשים, like a partition that is not a vessel at all, so it has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not take effect / does not help

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying a partition makes the oven pure. He is saying the partition counts for nothing. In the same way, חולין intent counts for nothing for a קרבן.

phrases.english: And he resolves:

phrases.aramaic: חוּלִּין אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים – כִּמְחִיצָה אֵצֶל תַּנּוּר;
phrases.english: Non-sacred relative to sacred is like a partition relative to an oven;
just as a partition in an oven
does not take effect for it at all,
so too, non-sacred relative to sacred
does not take effect for it at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁנִּי: חוּלִּין אֵצֶל קָדָשִׁים כִּמְחִיצָה אֵצֶל תַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between רב's ruling on חטאת and the ברייתא about a כלי שטף inside a כלי חרס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between something of a related category and something totally foreign
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a כלי שטף is not 'of the kind' of כלי חרס yet still matters, anything foreign should matter, including חולין intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי שטף is still a vessel, but חולין is completely foreign to קדשים, like a partition in an oven that has no effect at all.

steps.title: Source: a divided oven is all impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that a partition inside an oven does not stop טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: an oven that was divided with boards or curtains, and a שרץ was found in one place, everything is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבא's claim that a partition does nothing inside an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven is a כלי חרס, and a שרץ in its airspace makes everything inside impure. Boards or curtains are not vessels, so they do not split the oven into separate parts. Food on the other side of the divider still becomes impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping animal, which makes things impure

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
An oven that one divided
with boards or with curtains,
and a creeping animal was found in one place,
everything is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: תַּנּוּר שֶׁחֲצָצוֹ בִּנְסָרִים אוֹ בִּירִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה behind רבא's comparison to a partition in an oven.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a partition inside an oven has no effect at all
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about an oven divided with boards or curtains

steps.title: A broken barrel hanging inside the oven
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: a broken barrel plugged with straw does not protect its food from a שרץ in the oven, but רבי אליעזר says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A barrel that is broken, plugged with straw, and lowered into the oven's airspace: if a שרץ is inside the barrel, the oven is impure. If a שרץ is in the oven, the food inside the barrel is impure. And רבי אליעזר says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה, which now brings a second case of something hanging inside an oven. Here a מחלוקת opens between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken barrel is no longer a proper vessel, even if it is plugged with straw. So the תנא קמא treats it like the partition: it does not separate, and טומאה passes both ways. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says the food inside the barrel stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A round barrel or hive-shaped container

phrases.english: A barrel that is broken
and plugged up with straw,
and lowered into the airspace of the oven:
if a creeping animal is inside it, the oven is impure;
if a creeping animal is in the oven,
the food inside it is impure.
And Rabbi Eliezer deems it pure.
phrases.notes: He means the food inside the barrel stays pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה with a second case and a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a broken barrel plugged with straw does not block טומאה between it and the oven. רבי אליעזר rules the food inside it pure.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר proves his view: if such a container protects against the severe טומאת מת, it should surely protect inside a כלי חרס, which is milder.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: it is a קל וחומר! If it protects in the case of a dead body, which is severe, shouldn't it protect inside an earthenware vessel, which is mild?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a reason for his opinion that the food inside the barrel stays pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת is stricter than the טומאה of a שרץ inside a כלי חרס. רבי אליעזר argues that if this kind of barrel can protect against the strict one, it should surely protect against the milder one.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
A dead body (the most severe source of טומאה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא compares חולין to a partition in an oven: it is not a vessel at all, so it has no effect. The source משנה shows a partition does not stop טומאה in an oven. In the broken barrel case, רבי אליעזר disagrees and uses a קל וחומר from טומאת מת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: It is an a fortiori argument!
If it protected in the case of a corpse, which is severe,
shall it not protect in an earthenware vessel, which is lenient?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אליעזר's reasoning for ruling the food in the barrel pure.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the food inside the broken barrel stays pure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from protection against טומאת מת

steps.title: The Rabbis reject רבי אליעזר's proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond to רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר by saying 'No,' signaling that his logical proof does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים in the משנה start to push back on רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר by flatly saying 'No.' This line sets up the next move, where they will explain why his proof fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר argued that if a plugged container protects against the stronger טומאת מת, it should surely protect against the milder טומאה inside a כלי חרס. The חכמים's 'No' means they do not accept this logic. Their reason is not given yet. It comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: No. A standard opening for rejecting a קל וחומר
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (or the reverse)

steps.confusionAlert: This 'No' does not yet tell you why the proof fails. Don't decide the reason on your own; the חכמים explain it in the very next line.

phrases.english: They said to him: No;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קל וחומר that רבי אליעזר brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from טומאת מת to a כלי חרס inside an oven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet. The חכמים only announce their rejection here, and their explanation follows in the next line.
